articles.title: GREETINGS FROM ARUBA
articles.summary: SJAA members traveled to Aruba to observe a recent solar eclipse, initially facing overcast skies and rain. Despite early challenges, the weather cleared 45 minutes before totality, allowing them to witness a nearly 3-minute-40-second event, featuring a diamond ring, solar corona with streamers and prominences, and visible planets like Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury.

articles.title: APRIL
articles.summary: The provided content outlines a schedule of astronomical events and meetings for the month of April. It includes several star parties at various locations like Houge Park and Fremont Peak, a general meeting with a swap/auction, and an astronomy class focusing on star charts. Key details like sunset times, moon phases, and clock changes are also noted for the respective dates.

articles.title: MAY
articles.summary: This document outlines the astronomy-related events scheduled for the month of May, primarily hosted by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). Key activities include multiple star parties at Houge Park and Fremont Peak, an Astronomy Day celebration, a 'Lunar Observing' class, and a general meeting. It also mentions the Riverside Telescope Maker's Conference and provides contact information for the SJAA.

articles.title: TOTAL SOLAR ECLIPSE
articles.summary: This article recounts the observation of the February 26, 1998, total solar eclipse from the Celebrity Cruise line ship M/V Galaxy near Antigua. Despite initial gloomy, overcast, and rainy weather, the ship found a clearing, allowing passengers a clear view of the partially-eclipsed Sun at first contact and mideclipse. The report also notes some tension regarding observing site allocations among passengers.

articles.title: Aruba, from p. 1
articles.summary: The author recounts a "perfect experience" in Aruba, where many cruise ships pursued the centerline of a celestial event, strongly implying an eclipse viewing. Despite initial hesitation, the author praises Aruba's beautiful beaches, great food, and friendly people. Having now witnessed three such events, the author is already planning for another eclipse in Istanbul in August 1999.

articles.title: From Tom Frayne:
articles.summary: Tom Frayne recounts their experience observing a solar eclipse, initially facing challenges with cloud cover and a time zone error in their star map program. Despite the obstacles, they successfully viewed and photographed totality, witnessing the corona, prominences, Mercury, and Jupiter, much to the excitement of themselves and passers-by. The experience was described as spectacular, with observers expressing awe and emotion.

articles.title: From Bill Arnett:
articles.summary: Bill Arnett successfully observed a total solar eclipse from a cruise ship, despite initial 50% cloud cover. The ship's captain utilized weather radar to perform a crucial maneuver 20 minutes before totality, finding a clear hole in the clouds. Arnett highly recommends cruising for eclipses, praising the ship and overall trip experience.

articles.title: From Gary Mitchell:
articles.summary: This article features two personal accounts of observing the February 1998 total solar eclipse from a cruise ship near Aruba. Gary Mitchell details his successful first astrophotography attempt, capturing the eclipse's phases and learning about automation, while emphasizing the visual grandeur of the corona and prominences. Separately, Duane Sand recounts his memorable proposal to Christina C. immediately after the eclipse's second 'diamond ring,' tying the celestial event to their engagement.

articles.title: FREMONT PEAK DISASTER
articles.summary: The 30" Challenger telescope at Fremont Peak sustained approximately $10,000 in storm damage, posing a significant setback for Bay Area astronomy. The Fremont Peak Observatory Association (FPOA) is appealing for private donations and volunteer "sweat equity" to repair and restore the vital instrument. An initial $1000 has been pledged, and the FPOA treasurer's contact information is provided for those willing to contribute.

articles.title: Eclipse, from p. 1
articles.summary: This article details a solar eclipse observation from a ship, where the observer struggled to photograph totality due to significant ship motion but managed to capture partial phases. Despite photographic challenges, the observer enjoyed the visual experience, noting visible planets, stars, and solar prominences, and comparing the temperature drop and rapid onset/end of totality to a previous 1991 eclipse. The author highly recommends naked-eye viewing and expresses excitement for a future eclipse.

articles.title: AUCTION & SWAP MEET
articles.summary: The article describes the annual SJAA "Auction & Swap Meet" event, humorously dubbed "Transfer Of Various Projects From One Garage To Another," scheduled for April 4. This event draws attendees from across northern California, offering a swap meet starting at noon and an auction led by Jay Freeman beginning at 4pm. It's highlighted as a great opportunity for the astronomical community to buy or sell equipment, find bargains, and network.

articles.title: PERIODICAL PUBLICATION STATEMENT
articles.summary: The document is a formal periodical publication statement for the "SJAA Ephemeris," the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It specifies that the newsletter is published 12 times a year, from January through December. The statement also includes the full mailing address for the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: SUBMIT
articles.summary: Members are encouraged to submit articles for publication in the *SJAA Ephemeris* newsletter. Submissions should be emailed to Dave North at Timocharis@aol.com by the tenth of the month to be considered for the following issue, and must include the author's name and phone number.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: This article details optimal lunar observing opportunities for April, noting that early April (especially days 3-5) offers excellent views of the first quarter moon, even surpassing March in some aspects. Key events include a strong eastern libration on April 3, making certain eastern maria prominent, and a close conjunction of the Moon with Venus and Jupiter on April 23. It also highlights specific features to observe, such as sunrise over Sinus Iridium and the west limb on the 19th.

articles.title: AANC ANNUAL CONFERENCE: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE
articles.summary: The AANC Annual Conference, "Life in the Universe," was held on April 11, 1998, at the Lawrence Hall of Science at UC Berkeley. The workshop featured renowned speakers including Dr. Jill Tarter (Project Phoenix), Chris McKay (NASA Ames), and Andrew Fraknoi, discussing topics ranging from the search for intelligent life and possibilities of life on Mars and Europa, to exoplanet discoveries.

articles.title: Registration fees:
articles.summary: This document outlines registration fees for an upcoming event, detailing rates for advance purchase ($20.00), youth aged 11-18 ($12.00), and at-door registration ($25.00). It also notes potential small fees for parking and an optional $8.00 lunch, directing attendees to a website for updates and providing fax and mail options for form submission.

articles.title: Jay Freeman
articles.summary: An amateur astronomer recounts a favorable observation of the Moon's west limb in February 1998, using a small refractor to glimpse Mare Orientale on the far side due to extreme libration. The article also provides a technical explanation of apochromatic refractors, distinguishing them from achromats and stressing that actual color correction performance is more crucial than the design label, citing historical examples of apochromats with poor visual performance.

articles.title: Astronomy Education Resource Book Organizer
articles.summary: Project ASTRO at the Astronomical Society of the Pacific is seeking a qualified individual for a three-month summer position. The role involves compiling, evaluating, and rewriting an updated edition of their "Universe at Your Fingertips" astronomy education resource notebook for grades 4-9. Candidates should possess a background in both astronomy and education, along with strong writing skills, to work in San Francisco.

articles.title: YOSEMITE STAR PARTY
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is organizing a star party at Yosemite National Park on June 26-27, 1998. Participants will camp at Bridalveil camp, and are required to bring one instrument for every two people to set up for public viewing. The event is limited to 30 people, and details on attendance, rules, and observing conditions (including moon phase and twilight times) are provided.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: The article provides updates on two comets: Hale-Bopp, which is slowly dimming in the southern sky but still displaying a short tail, and Meunier-Dupouy, continuing its travel in the morning sky; both are approximately three astronomical units away. It also includes a note on comet hunting, highlighting that only one of 100 visual discoveries since 1975 was made without a reflector, refractor, or binoculars, specifically Merlin Kohler's 1977 find using an 8" Schmidt-Cassegrain.

articles.title: Ephemerides (for 0h UT)
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for two comets, C/1997 J2 (Meunier-Dupouy) and C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), for dates ranging from early April to mid-May. For each comet, the data includes Right Ascension, Declination, elongation from the Sun, and apparent magnitude, all specified for 0h UT.

articles.title: Orbital Elements
articles.summary: This document presents a detailed table of orbital elements for two comets, Hale-Bopp and Meunier-Dupouy. It lists various parameters for each, including perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, orbital period, and absolute magnitude. The data is referenced from MPC 30738 and includes contact information for Don Machholz.

articles.title: On Storing Eyepieces:
articles.summary: This short article humorously discusses casual methods of storing inexpensive eyepieces, such as in a pocket or on a car dashboard. The author expresses a lighthearted concern for avoiding contamination with various odd items and mentions using the car to allow eyepieces to undew.

articles.title: THE SHALLOW SKY
articles.summary: This April 1998 observing guide indicates poor conditions for planet-watching as most planets are too close to the sun, though a close grouping of the crescent moon, Venus, and Jupiter may be visible on April 23rd. The Lyrids meteor shower peaks on April 21-22, and the Eta Aquarids, associated with Halley's Comet, become observable from mid-April.

articles.title: Lunar
articles.summary: This document provides a detailed schedule of lunar phases for a given month, including the exact times and dates for First Quarter, Full Moon, Last Quarter, and New Moon. It also lists the corresponding rise, transit, and set times for the Moon, clarifying the use of Standard and Daylight Savings Time.

articles.title: Mercury
articles.summary: This document presents an astronomical ephemeris for the planet Mercury, detailing its position and visibility for three specific dates. It includes data points such as rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension, Declination, apparent magnitude, and distance from the Sun in Astronomical Units.

articles.title: Venus
articles.summary: This document presents an ephemeris for Venus, providing key astronomical data for three distinct dates within a month. It lists the planet's magnitude and distance from Earth, alongside its rise, transit, and set times, as well as its right ascension and declination coordinates, useful for observation planning.

articles.title: Mars
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical ephemeris for Mars, detailing its rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension (R.A.) and Declination (Dec.) for the 7th, 17th, and 27th of a given month. It also lists Mars's distance from Earth at 2.43 A.U. and its apparent magnitude at +1.3.

articles.title: Jupiter
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for Jupiter, detailing its rise, transit, and set times, along with its right ascension and declination for three dates in the month (7th, 17th, 27th). It also lists Jupiter's distance at 5.71 A.U. and its magnitude at -2.2, serving as a guide for observers.

articles.title: Saturn
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for Saturn, including its distance (10.3 A.U.) and visual magnitude (+1.0). It lists ephemeris information for three dates in a specific month, detailing rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension (R.A.) and Declination (Dec.). This data is crucial for observers tracking Saturn's position in the sky.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V Intelligent Life in System?
articles.summary: The article, titled "SOL Star Type G2V Intelligent Life in System?", primarily presents a table of astronomical data. This data includes specific rise, transit, and set times alongside Right Ascension and Declination coordinates for various dates. Additionally, it defines "HOD" as "Base of Darkness," but offers no further discussion on intelligent life or the G2V star type itself beyond the title's query.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document presents a table detailing the begin and end times of astronomical twilight for several specific Julian Dates. This information is crucial for astronomers to determine when the sky is sufficiently dark for optimal deep-sky observations, marking the period when the sun is between 12 and 18 degrees below the horizon.

articles.title: Siderealtime
articles.summary: This document, titled 'Siderealtime', presents a tabular format displaying numerical values for 'Transit Right Ascension' and 'Local Midnit' in relation to sidereal time. It appears to be a reference or calculation aid for determining sidereal time based on these astronomical parameters.

articles.title: Darkest Saturday Night 25-April-98
articles.summary: This document provides specific astronomical times for Saturday, April 25, 1998, highlighted as a "Darkest Saturday Night." It lists key celestial events including sunset, twilight end, moonset, and dawn begin, indicating a period conducive to dark-sky observation.

articles.title: ACTIVITIES THROUGH OTHER CLUBS
articles.summary: The article outlines various astronomy activities and viewing opportunities hosted by different clubs. TAC maintains a standing reservation at Montebello for Wednesday observing sessions and organizes mobile or Van Meter star parties on Fridays, with details found on their website. Additionally, PAS offers public viewing at Foothill Observatory every clear Friday evening and solar viewing every clear Saturday morning, encouraging participation from SJAA members.

articles.title: April
articles.summary: This document lists the astronomical events scheduled for April, including a Peninsula Astronomical Society (PAS) general meeting on April 10 featuring a "Total Solar Eclipse" topic. Other events are a PAS board meeting on April 15 and an HVAG Star Party at Grant Ranch on April 25, taking place at Foothill College and Grant Ranch respectively.

articles.title: May
articles.summary: The document outlines two key meetings for PAS members in May. A General Meeting is scheduled for May 8th at 7:30 pm at Foothill College, followed by a Board Meeting on May 13th at 7:30 pm at the Foothill College Observatory.

articles.title: DIRECTIONS TO SJAA PLACES
articles.summary: This document provides detailed driving directions to three key locations for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA): Houge Park, Henry Coe State Park, and Fremont Peak State Park. It includes specific routes from major highways and notes entrance fees for the state parks. The information appears to be an excerpt from an "SJAA EPHEMERIS" dated April 1998.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: This article discusses content for the monthly 'Ephemeris,' including reports on a Caribbean eclipse and meteor activity. It also covers recent club elections, acknowledging the outgoing President Jack Zeiders, and details a successful star party at Houge Park. Finally, it presents results from a poll regarding electronic versus paper delivery of the 'Ephemeris,' showing a preference for electronic versions while assuring the continuation of paper copies.

articles.title: Bill Arnett
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) held a board meeting where Bill Arnett agreed to assist the Secretary, discussed a $400 loss for 1997, and considered preliminary bylaw changes. Immediately following, the annual membership meeting was conducted where four new Board of Directors, including Bill Arnett, Mark Taylor, Terry Kahl, and Mike Koop, were elected by acclamation.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and members of the Board of Directors for an unspecified organization. It includes the names of the President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, and several Directors, along with their respective phone numbers.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: The article lists the staff members for "Ephemeris", detailing their specific roles and contact information. Key positions include Editor, Circulation (with two contacts), Layout, and Proofing, each assigned to an individual.

articles.title: Mike Koop
articles.summary: Paul Barton has retired from the Telescope Loan Program after a decade of dedicated service. The article expresses gratitude for his hard work and vision, anticipating continued consultation with him.

articles.title: Scope Loans
articles.summary: The document, titled "Scope Loans," provides a detailed list of astronomical telescopes currently on loan. It specifies the description of each scope (e.g., 4.5" Newt, 14" Dobson, C8), the name of the borrower, and the corresponding due date for its return. This appears to be an internal tracking record for an equipment loan program.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists extended loans of various telescopes and associated equipment. It includes details such as the scope description, the borrower's name, and the due date, with some loans marked as 'Indefinite' or having specific notes.

articles.title: Availible Scopes
articles.summary: The document provides a simple inventory of three available telescopes: an 11" Dobson, a 13" Dobson, and a 7" f/9 Newtonian/Pipe Mount. It lists the current storage location for each scope, indicating individuals responsible for them.

articles.title: Waiting List
articles.summary: This document, titled "Waiting List," outlines astronomical equipment (specifically an 8" Celestron S/C and a C8 for astrophotography) available to members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It lists members currently on standby for these scopes and includes a request for members with space to store equipment. SJAA members can reserve any available scope by contacting Mike Koop.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) membership form, detailing options for new or renewal memberships, including standard and junior rates, and an optional Sky & Telescope subscription. It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment to the treasurer, along with contact information for the association.
